conventions.convention: Full AC is assumed throughout. Knot Seifert surfaces are connected compact smooth oriented embedded surfaces with the prescribed oriented boundary; their Euler characteristic is 1−2g.
Vij = lk(ai+, aj) uses the positive normal; t acts by the positive-meridian deck transformation. The presentation matrix is V−tVᵀ.
The polynomial ΔK generates E0 of absolute Alexander homology and is defined up to ±t^k. The empty matrix has determinant 1. The separate fraction is DK = ΔK/(1−t).
Degree means Laurent exponent width, not greatest exponent. The unique symmetric associate has value 1 at t=1.
A positive Hopf band has induced boundary linking +1 and core self-pairing −1. The ordered plumbing cores have intersection +1 and V12=0.

load_bearing.statement: Under full AC and the stated smooth oriented knot, connected Seifert surface, integral basis, positive-normal and positive-meridian conventions, E0(AK) = (det(V−tVᵀ)). The empty determinant is 1; det(V−Vᵀ)=±1, and every generator ΔK satisfies ΔK(1)=±1. These assertions are compatible with integral basis changes and orientation-preserving ambient isotopies of knot-surface pairs.

Assume full AC. For every smooth oriented knot, connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface and ordered integral homology basis in the stated positive-push convention, det(V−tVᵀ) differs from ΔK by a unit ±t^k. The determinant is 1 for the empty matrix. The formula concerns ΔK, separately from DK=ΔK/(1−t).

Assume full AC. Every Alexander generator of a smooth oriented knot satisfies ΔK(1)=±1, reciprocity up to ±t^k, and exponent width at most 2g(K). There is a unique symmetric associate with value 1 at t=1, supported in [−g(K),g(K)]. The fraction ΔK/(1−t) has a simple pole at t=1.

Assume full AC. For smooth oriented knots K,J and their connected sum using the fixed gluing convention, Δ(K#J) differs from ΔKΔJ by a Laurent unit. The statement is independent of local connected-sum choices and of the computing surfaces and bases.

seams_checked.note: The positive-push matrix, positive-meridian presentation, unimodular skew part and transported-basis congruence match the supplier statements. Full AC is retained.
The multiplicativity proof uses the fixed oriented gluing and independence of sufficiently small coordinate-ball, subarc and frame choices. It explicitly selects such coordinate balls.
Root-product and double-cover consumers use the determinant only up to ±t^k; absolute values at roots of unity remove that ambiguity. Oddness at −1 uses Δ(1)=±1 correctly.
The singular-set calculation preserves the determinant convention and derives reciprocity directly. Conway and Arf consumers use the unique symmetric normalization with value one.
Both examples use exactly the supplied negative-diagonal trefoil and mixed-diagonal figure-eight matrices. Their signatures, Alexander-root test and Conway normalizations agree.
The genus formula uses exponent width ≤2g(K), retaining full AC and treating unit-slope knots separately.
No direct citation of an assigned item was found in this page's item bodies. Its trefoil plumbing and rational-form calculations agree with the batch's matrix and normalization conventions.
Factorization and signature-vanishing consumers use Δ as the unit associate of det(V−tVᵀ), retaining full AC. The factorization statement explicitly distinguishes Δ from Δ/(1−t).

The Alexander-one reduction correctly obtains a Laurent-unit determinant for each supplied Seifert matrix from ΔK associated to 1. The outside proof-formatting alert does not concern citation fidelity.
